title: Aurora
name: Aurora
metaDescription: Aurora 1031 exchange guidance for medical office near Anschutz, E-470 industrial, and adaptive-reuse retail in Colorado's third-largest city.

sections.html: Aurora sits directly east of Denver and sprawls across three counties, which makes it Colorado's third-largest city by population even though most people outside the metro have never heard of it. The commercial inventory here runs wide, medical campus buildings, industrial along E-470, retail power centers, and it doesn't behave like a single tight submarket.

sections.heading: The Anschutz Medical Campus Effect
sections.html:
The Anschutz Medical Campus and the surrounding Fitzsimons redevelopment turned a decommissioned Army hospital site into one of the largest academic medical and research campuses in the country. That pulls real demand for medical office, lab, and research flex space in the blocks around it, demand that has nothing to do with the rest of Aurora's retail and industrial stock. A buyer looking at medical office near Fitzsimons should treat it as its own micro-market, not a generic Aurora comp.

The scale of Aurora is worth saying plainly: it spans Adams, Arapahoe, and Douglas counties, three separate taxing and permitting jurisdictions under one city government. A buyer needs to confirm which county a specific parcel falls in before assuming a property tax rate or a permitting timeline, since those numbers can differ meaningfully from one side of the city to the other.

sections.heading: What's Actually on This Identification List
sections.html:
Realistic property types coming out of Aurora right now:

  • medical office and research flex space near the Anschutz Medical Campus
  • industrial and distribution buildings along the E-470 and Tower Road corridor
  • retail power centers and pad sites near Town Center at Aurora
  • adaptive-reuse retail and event space in converted industrial buildings

sections.heading: Industrial Along the Beltway
sections.html:
The E-470 toll corridor on Aurora's east side has pulled in distribution and logistics buildings looking for beltway access without downtown Denver's congestion. Buckley Space Force Base sits nearby too and brings a stable base of military and contractor workforce that supports housing and retail demand on that side of the city in a way that isn't tied to the broader metro economy.

Stanley Marketplace is worth knowing about specifically. It's a former aircraft parts hangar converted into a food-and-retail hall, and it shows what adaptive reuse can do with the right industrial shell in this city. Not every warehouse converts that cleanly, but it's a real comp for anyone underwriting a similar reuse play.

Aurora's East Colfax corridor also carries a distinct retail identity, small international grocery stores, family-run restaurants, and immigrant- and refugee-owned businesses that serve one of the more diverse populations in the metro. Lease terms and tenant credit on that stretch look different than a national-brand power center near Town Center at Aurora, and a buyer should underwrite it on its own terms rather than comping it against big-box retail elsewhere in the city.

sections.heading: Diligence Points for This Market
sections.html: Confirm which micro-market a property actually sits in before comping it against a citywide average, medical office near Anschutz, industrial near E-470, and retail near Town Center at Aurora all trade on different fundamentals. Check flood zone status on anything near Sand Creek or the South Platte tributaries, and confirm any military-adjacent zoning restrictions near Buckley before assuming a use is by-right.

sections.heading: Positioning an Aurora Identification
sections.html: Given Aurora's size and the spread between its micro-markets, a single Aurora property can carry real weight on an identification list, especially a medical office asset near Anschutz. Investors coordinating a 1031 into Aurora often pair a medical or industrial asset here with a downtown Denver or DTC candidate as a backup, since the two markets don't move on the same drivers. A qualified intermediary should confirm early which specific taxing jurisdiction and municipal review process applies to the Aurora parcel on the list, since that paperwork can take longer to assemble than for a single-jurisdiction suburb closer to the core of the Denver metro. T-12 financial review on any Aurora retail or medical asset should note which micro-market the trailing income actually reflects, since a rent roll pulled from a Fitzsimons-area building tells a buyer nothing reliable about a Town Center at Aurora retail parcel five miles away. A replacement property identification for Aurora should note the exact submarket by name in the paperwork, rather than only the city, since that specificity matters if a lender or a tax advisor needs to reconstruct the deal's reasoning later.

faqs.q: Is medical office near the Anschutz Medical Campus a strong 1031 replacement property?
faqs.a: It can be, given the scale of the academic medical campus driving demand. Treat it as its own micro-market rather than comping it against generic Aurora retail or industrial.

faqs.q: Why does industrial property cluster along E-470 in Aurora?
faqs.a: Beltway access without downtown Denver congestion is the draw. Distribution and logistics tenants have gravitated to that corridor for exactly that reason.

faqs.q: Does Buckley Space Force Base affect nearby commercial property?
faqs.a: Yes, it supports a stable military and contractor workforce base for nearby housing and retail, largely independent of the broader metro economy. Confirm any base-adjacent zoning restrictions before assuming a use is allowed.

faqs.q: What is Stanley Marketplace and why does it come up in Aurora deals?
faqs.a: It's a converted aircraft parts hangar turned food-and-retail hall, and it's the reference point buyers use when underwriting a similar industrial-to-retail adaptive reuse project in this city.

faqs.q: Can one Aurora property carry a full three-property identification list?
faqs.a: A medical office asset near Anschutz can carry real weight given the scale of that campus, but most buyers still pair it with a downtown Denver or DTC asset since Aurora's submarkets don't move together.
